keyFindings.text: **F1 (P1, root cause — hypothesis CONFIRMED with a decisive refinement).** The claim listener survives from the pre-trust pass into the trusted pass on the shared per-loader event bus, and every final-pass copy stands down. The refinement: the copy that wins the claim is the **user-scope symlink alias** (`~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-fast-mode-w-subagent-support` → main checkout) loaded by the untrusted pre-trust pass, not any project copy. Real-run trace: one `on` (pass A claim) then one `emit` with `listeners=1` (pass B probe → marked claimed → stand-down).

**F2 (P1, the zero-flag mechanism).** In the trusted main checkout the alias is **pruned from the final set** by realpath dedupe (alias realpath == project copy realpath; project scope outranks user scope), so the claimed+flagged pass-A entry is discarded while the surviving project copy stood down → zero `--fast`. Final set: 31 extensions, single flagless fast-mode entry. In a worktree the alias realpath (main checkout) differs from the worktree copy, so BOTH entries survive; the pass-A alias entry keeps `flags=[fast]` → exactly one. This explains all four observed counts, including `-a`/`-na` (single-pass, no pre-trust listener, project copy claims).

**F3 (P1, blast radius).** In the trusted main checkout the stand-down kills the whole extension, not just the flag: the factory returns before `/fast` command registration, status handling and session-start wiring (same early return at src/index.ts:123-124). Inference from the confirmed early return; flag absence is directly observed.

**F4 (P2).** The extension source comment's model ("Pi ... fails the whole load when two copies register one flag") is contradicted by the loader: conflicts are reported as diagnostics and "precedence is handled by load order" [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/resource-loader.js:583-585].

**F5 (P2, claim design).** Recommended design — **gate only side effects on the claim; register the flag before/outside the claim early-return** (minimal change to `claimPackage` usage). Verified by mechanics against all four observed layouts: main trusted → dedupe leaves only the project copy, which registers unconditionally (exactly 1, no conflict); worktree trusted → alias entry + worktree copy both register, conflict is a diagnostic and load-order precedence (project rank 0 first) makes the worktree copy the effective one; untrusted → only the alias copy loads and registers; `-a`/`-na` → single pass, project/worktree copy claims and registers. Residual: `/fast` and other side-effect registrations stay claim-gated, so in the trusted main checkout they remain dead until the deeper fix; full-unconditional registration (drop the claim) fixes everything but runs both copies' handlers in coexistence layouts.

**F6 (P2, upstream fix path).** Pi-side options: release pre-trust event-bus subscriptions when `reload()` discards the pre-trust set, or have `loadFinalExtensionSet` prefer a final-pass copy over a pruned-path preloaded claim. Runtime-scoping will NOT fix it: the final pass reuses the pre-trust runtime [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/resource-loader.js:560,577].

**F7 (P3, ruled out).** Release-on-`project_trust` claim design: refuted in sandbox (the internally re-run pre-trust pass re-claims and is pruned again). Realpath-keyed claims with same-file takeover: fragile across a second `reload()` on the same loader (stale listeners re-mark fresh probes); not recommended without an eviction primitive.

Observation (method): a harness that calls `loadProjectTrustExtensions()` and then `reload({resolveProjectTrust})` runs the pre-trust pass TWICE and distorts which copy claims; real runs run it exactly once inside `reload()`.

**F-01 (P2, mechanism closed).** The "reappeared" generator: `render-command-contract.cjs` re-created `.skilled/commands/deep/assets/compiled/` (now holding only `manifest.jsonl`) on every live render between phase 004 and `59565c1849`, because `appendManifestRow` mkdir-recurses before appending [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/render-command-contract.cjs:138-140]. `59565c1849` repointed the writer, the projection-manifest seed [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/legacy-projections/legacy-projection-manifest.ts:200], the README snippet [SOURCE: .skilled/command-support/deep/assets/compiled/README.md:112] and the gitignore rule [SOURCE: .gitignore:202] to `.skilled/command-support/deep/assets/compiled/manifest.jsonl`. A post-fix live render lands there with exit 0 and the old directory absent [SOURCE: specs/cli-external-orchestration/082-opencode-v1-v2-dual-compat/009-sk-code-opencode-alignment/scratch/gates/render-manifest-live.txt:1-5].

**F-02 (P3, orphaned data, not regeneration).** The main checkout's untracked `manifest.jsonl` (mtime 2026-07-13, never tracked by any commit) predates the merge entirely; nothing regenerated it and the old path is written and read by nothing in the merged main. It became status-visible only because `59565c1849` retired the old-path gitignore rule. It is inert on both versions (non-markdown) but is stale pre-move data sitting inside the live command tree and makes the main checkout's tree diverge from fresh clones.

**F-03 (P2, registration semantics + residual watch-items).** No non-command file registers as a command on OpenCode 1.19.3 or 2.0.32 after the move: both scan the symlinked single tree and register markdown only (12 non-command `.md` registered before the move — the actual pre-merge defect; v2 isolated listing `commands: 41`, `moved-file entries: []` [SOURCE: specs/cli-external-orchestration/082-opencode-v1-v2-dual-compat/004-agents-commands-config/scratch/v2-command-isolated.txt:2-3], v1 parity at REQ-006 [SOURCE: specs/cli-external-orchestration/082-opencode-v1-v2-dual-compat/004-agents-commands-config/spec.md:158]). Listings additionally include non-tree builtin entries (`init`, `review`) and the v2 nested-worktree superset effect from ancestor `.opencode` merging [SOURCE: specs/cli-external-orchestration/082-opencode-v1-v2-dual-compat/004-agents-commands-config/spec.md:134].

**F-04 (P2, parity + generator enumeration).** Every dual-read surface reads the same on both versions: `.opencode/commands` and `.opencode/agents` are symlinks to `.skilled/*` (single file set, `diff -rq` zero differences); `opencode.json` keeps the v1 shape which OpenCode 2 converts on load, guarded by `.skilled/bin/tests/opencode-config-shape.test.cjs` against v2-only keys [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/tests/opencode-config-shape.test.cjs:15-19]; agent mirrors were synced and checker-verified in phase 004. Fixed-list sweep across generators/validators closes clean: `compile-command-contracts.cjs` writes its targets from the command-support base [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/compile-command-contracts.cjs:699], and `validate-command-references.cjs` walks directories dynamically with only `README.md`/`.contract.md` skips [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/scripts/validate-command-references.cjs:201].

**F-05 (P3, remediation bundle).** (1) Delete the orphaned untracked `.skilled/commands/deep/assets/compiled/` in the main checkout; no gitignore re-entry needed. (2) Keep the `59565c1849` relocation as merged. (3) Normalize doctor/listing checks: subtract builtin entries (`init`, `review`) and account for v2's ancestor walk-up so nested vs isolated listings compare like-for-like. (4) Later polish: consider relocating the per-render manifest append out of the `.skilled` source tree into a build/state directory, per the sk-code-skilled contract that the commands tree holds only commands — current placement works (gitignored, gate-verified), so this is hygiene, not a bug.

**F-06 (P3, premise correction for the packet record).** The focus's premise that the manifest "reappeared" is materially corrected: the file itself was never removed (never tracked), while the *directory* is what transiently reappeared — the renderer re-created it between 004 and 59565c1849 whenever a live render ran, and any checkout with such a render in that window still carries a fresh-looking folder. In the main checkout the surviving file predates the merge (Jul 13 mtime), so no render replenished it there.
**cli dispatch** — the `opencode-version.cjs` version resolver plus per-version argv documentation and a doctor battery that parses `--version` rather than pinning.

**Commands/agents/config** — single shared trees via symlinks (`.opencode/commands` → `.skilled/commands`, same for agents) plus the v1-shape `opencode.json` that OpenCode 2 converts on load, guarded against v2-only keys by the config-shape test.
**Plugins** — the `dualPlugin` bridge (`lib/v2-bridge.js`): mapped hook set, event aliases, two synthesized stream→event mappings, `skippedKeys` accounting.
**Provisioning** — `worktree-provision-paths.txt` driving `provision_worktree` (bun vs npm choice, lockfile-frozen installs).

**Q2 stays open**, deliberately. Its plugins/tests/generators limbs are now enumerated (plugins: 16/16 bridged + one designed exception; tests: the two pinned arrays, README:77, the provision list; generators: closed clean by 59565c1849 with dynamic walkers verified), and the cli-opencode doc drift is enumerated by 016. What remains is breadth: ~227 changed docs outside 018's focus set have their own mode validators but have not been swept for OpenCode-version assumptions. A box ticked now would overstate the run.

Listings: doctor/listing batteries subtract the non-tree builtins (`init`, `review`) and normalize OpenCode 2's ancestor `.opencode` walk-up before comparing.

Plugins: a `plugin-inventory` module `readdir`s `.opencode/plugins`, classifies entries (regular `.js` = bridge consumer; symlink/dist bundle = native-dual exception), feeds both v2 suites, and is checked both ways (unlisted entry fails; manifest entry naming a missing file fails).
